intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the legendary Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from local vendors. Engage with longtime merchants and discover the heart of Tokyo's food culture in one of the world's most famous market districts.

experiences.name: Akihabara Electric Town Tech & Culture Immersion
experiences.description: Dive deep into Tokyo's iconic tech and otaku hub. Browse multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera, visit retro game shops, explore maid cafes, and discover the latest in gadgets, robotics, and anime merchandise. A must-do for anyone fascinated by Japanese tech culture.

experiences.name: Ramen Alley Crawl in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Navigate the narrow, atmospheric lanes of Shinjuku's Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) and nearby ramen shops to taste regional ramen styles including tonkotsu, shoyu, and miso. Chat with local chefs and experience the authentic izakaya atmosphere that defines Tokyo's night food scene.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Experience one of the world's most celebrated digital art installations where technology and creativity merge. Walk through immersive, ever-changing rooms of interactive light, sound, and projection art created by the pioneering art collective teamLab. A perfect fusion of tech culture and artistic wonder.

experiences.name: Depachika Gourmet Basement Food Hall Experience
experiences.description: Descend into the legendary basement food halls (depachika) of Isetan or Takashimaya department stores in Shinjuku. Sample artisan wagashi sweets, premium bento boxes, handcrafted chocolates, and regional Japanese delicacies. A uniquely Japanese culinary tradition that showcases the country's obsession with food quality and presentation.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit from airport to hotel in Tsukiji.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Tsukiji boutique stay, freshen up, then take a short walk to explore the outer Tsukiji Market area. Browse the famous Tsukiji Outer Market stalls selling fresh seafood snacks, tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette), and street food. Get oriented with the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sumida River waterfront near Tsukiji for a relaxing evening view. Visit the nearby Hamarikyu Gardens (entry ¥300) for a peaceful evening walk if time permits before closing at 17:00. Otherwise, explore the local convenience stores (7-Eleven, FamilyMart) to pick up budget essentials and Japanese snacks.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack on the plane.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Tsukiji Outer Market — try a fresh tuna onigiri or grilled scallop skewer for around ¥300–¥600.
meals.dinner: Ramen at a local Tsukiji ramen shop such as Tsukiji Shijo Ramen — hearty bowl for around ¥700–¥900.

day_by_day.notes: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for easy, discounted transit throughout Tokyo. Budget tip: convenience store meals are excellent quality and very affordable (¥400–¥700).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Outer Market early (opens around 5:00–6:00 AM) for the iconic breakfast experience. Try fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and seafood skewers directly from market vendors. This is one of Tokyo's most authentic local food experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Browse multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Akiba and Sofmap. Explore retro game shops, anime merchandise stores, and tech gadget stalls. Window shopping is free!
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara to explore the vibrant evening atmosphere. Visit multi-story arcades like SEGA or Taito Station — try retro arcade games for ¥100 per play. Walk through the neon-lit streets and observe Tokyo's unique otaku and tech culture.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh tuna sushi breakfast set for ¥800–¥1,200 at Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi (budget splurge worth it).
meals.lunch: Akihabara — try a set lunch (teishoku) at a local curry restaurant like CoCo Ichibanya for ¥700–¥900.
meals.dinner: Akihabara — budget gyudon (beef rice bowl) at Yoshinoya or Sukiya for ¥400–¥600.

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot. Most electronics stores open around 10:00–11:00 AM. Free Wi-Fi available in most major stores. Look for second-hand electronics shops for incredible bargains on tech gadgets.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Ueno Park (free entry) — one of Tokyo's largest and most beloved public parks. In mid-April, cherry blossoms may still be lingering. Visit the Ueno Zoo (¥600) or simply stroll through the park. Explore Ameyoko Market street nearby for cheap snacks, clothing, and goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Nature and Science in Ueno (¥630 entry) — excellent exhibits on technology, science, and Japanese innovation. Alternatively, explore the Tokyo National Museum (¥1,000) for cultural history.
day_by_day.evening: Take the subway to Asakusa — Tokyo's most traditional district. Walk the famous Nakamise Shopping Street leading to Senso-ji Temple. The temple is free and beautifully lit at night. Browse affordable souvenir shops along the street.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near the hotel — onigiri + coffee for ¥300–¥400.
meals.lunch: Ameyoko Market street food — grilled skewers, takoyaki, or a cheap bento for ¥500–¥700.
meals.dinner: Asakusa — try tempura at Asakusa Tempura Daikokuya or a budget tempura tendon set for ¥900–¥1,200.

day_by_day.notes: Ueno and Asakusa are connected and walkable or a short subway ride apart. Senso-ji is open 24 hours but the inner hall closes at 17:00. Fortune slips (omikuji) cost ¥100 — a fun cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shibuya — Tokyo's youth culture and fashion hub. Visit the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing, one of the world's busiest pedestrian crossings. Walk up to the free Shibuya Sky observation deck preview area or enjoy the crossing view from Starbucks overlooking it (buy a cheap drink).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Shibuya to Harajuku (15 minutes on foot). Explore Takeshita Street for quirky, affordable street fashion and crepes. Then walk through Yoyogi Park (free) — a great place to observe local Tokyo life on weekends, with musicians and picnickers.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Meiji Shrine in Harajuku (free entry, closes at sunset). Peaceful forested shrine in the heart of the city. Return to Shibuya for evening exploration — browse Don Quijote (discount store) for cheap souvenirs and snacks.

meals.breakfast: Grab a morning pastry and coffee at a local bakery in Tsukiji before heading out — around ¥400.
meals.lunch: Harajuku Takeshita Street — try a rainbow crepe or cheese dog for ¥500–¥700.
meals.dinner: Shibuya — budget sushi conveyor belt (kaiten-zushi) at Genki Sushi or Hamazushi for ¥800–¥1,200.

day_by_day.notes: Saturdays in Harajuku and Yoyogi Park are especially lively. Don Quijote in Shibuya is open late and is great for cheap snacks, cosmetics, and quirky Japanese goods. IC card transit makes hopping between areas very affordable.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island in Tokyo Bay. Take the scenic Yurikamome automated driverless monorail (great tech experience, use IC card). Explore teamLab Borderless digital art museum — book in advance, tickets around ¥3,200 but worth the splurge for a unique tech-art experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Odaiba — visit the free DiverCity Tokyo Plaza to see the giant life-size Gundam statue outside. Browse the futuristic shopping mall. Walk along the Odaiba waterfront for views of the Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward central Tokyo. Stop at Ginza (adjacent to Tsukiji) for a free evening window-shopping walk through Japan's most upscale shopping district. The architecture and storefronts are impressive even without spending money.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh fish breakfast or tamagoyaki for ¥400–¥700.
meals.lunch: Odaiba — food court lunch at DiverCity Tokyo for ¥700–¥1,000.
meals.dinner: Ginza — try a budget lunch special carried into evening at a nearby izakaya, or grab a bento from a Ginza convenience store for ¥500–¥700.

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless is a must for tech culture enthusiasts — book tickets online in advance to save time and ensure availability. The Yurikamome monorail itself is a fun automated transit experience worth enjoying.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shinjuku — Tokyo's busiest train station area and entertainment district. Visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (opens 9:30 AM) for panoramic 360-degree views of the city — completely free!
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden. Late April may still have late-blooming cherry blossoms or fresh spring greenery. Explore the traditional Japanese, French formal, and English landscape sections.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku at night — walk through Kabukicho entertainment district (safe to walk through, fascinating neon atmosphere). Explore the tiny atmospheric bars of Golden Gai (drinks from ¥500–¥800 per glass). This is quintessential Tokyo nightlife culture.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast — onigiri, yogurt, and coffee for ¥400.
meals.lunch: Shinjuku — try a cheap ramen at Ichiran Ramen (solo dining booths, unique experience) for ¥980–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Golden Gai area — grab yakitori skewers from a street stall or tiny izakaya for ¥800–¥1,200.

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building free observation deck is one of the best free views in Tokyo. Shinjuku Gyoen has a no-alcohol policy — good for a peaceful afternoon. Golden Gai bars are tiny (5–8 seats) and very atmospheric — some have cover charges of ¥500.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Akihabara for deeper tech culture exploration. Visit the Akihabara Radio Kaikan building — 10 floors of electronics components, vintage tech, and hobby goods. Explore the basement floors for electronic components beloved by makers and engineers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Maid Café district in Akihabara — a uniquely Japanese cultural experience. Many cafés offer a basic entry experience for ¥500–¥700 (budget one visit). Alternatively, visit the free Akihabara UDX building atrium for tech company showcases and events.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tsukiji area for a relaxed evening. Walk along the Sumida River and enjoy the city lights. Visit a local izakaya near Tsukiji for a budget dinner and drinks with locals.

meals.breakfast: Akihabara — pick up a morning pastry from a local bakery or convenience store for ¥300–¥400.
meals.lunch: Akihabara — try a lunch set at a local Japanese restaurant (teishoku) for ¥700–¥900.
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area izakaya — order a few small plates (yakitori, edamame, karaage) for ¥1,000–¥1,500 including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara Radio Kaikan is a paradise for tech enthusiasts — even browsing the component shops is fascinating. Check for any tech events or pop-up exhibitions happening in the area on this date.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old downtown (shitamachi) neighborhoods. Walk through Yanaka Ginza shopping street for local food stalls, traditional crafts, and an authentic non-touristy Tokyo experience. Visit Yanaka Cemetery for a peaceful walk among old cherry blossom trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nezu Shrine (free entry) — a beautiful vermillion torii gate pathway similar to Fushimi Inari in Kyoto but far less crowded. Walk through the tunnel of torii gates for a stunning photo opportunity. Continue to nearby Sendagi neighborhood for local café culture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ikebukuro — another major Tokyo hub with a slightly different character than Shibuya or Shinjuku. Visit Sunshine City (free to enter) and its aquarium if budget allows (¥2,400). Explore the Animate store — largest anime merchandise store in Japan.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza street food — try menchi katsu (fried meat cutlet) or croquette for ¥150–¥200 each.
meals.lunch: Yanaka area — local soba noodle restaurant for ¥700–¥900.
meals.dinner: Ikebukuro — budget Chinese-Japanese fusion at one of many affordable restaurants around the station for ¥700–¥1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is one of the most authentic neighborhoods in Tokyo — very few tourists, great local food, and a glimpse of old Tokyo atmosphere. Nezu Shrine is free and far less crowded than similar shrines elsewhere in Japan.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets in Toyosu (different from Borderless — book in advance, ¥3,200). A more intimate and immersive digital art and tech experience. Located in the Toyosu area near Tsukiji — very convenient from the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Toyosu Market (the new wholesale fish market that replaced Tsukiji's inner market). Take a free observation tour of the tuna auction viewing area (register in advance online). See the world's largest fish market in action from the viewing galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Walk back toward Tsukiji or take a short subway ride. Explore the築地 (Tsukiji) neighborhood at a leisurely pace — visit any remaining market stalls, try different street food you haven't tried yet.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — try a different vendor today, perhaps a fresh oyster or grilled squid for ¥400–¥600.
meals.lunch: Toyosu area — sushi lunch near the market for ¥1,000–¥1,500 (fresh fish at market prices).
meals.dinner: Tsukiji neighborhood — try a different local restaurant, perhaps tonkatsu (pork cutlet) set for ¥900–¥1,200.

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets tickets must be booked online in advance. Toyosu Market observation tours are free but require advance registration on the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website. Both are within easy reach of the Tsukiji hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's bohemian neighborhood known for vintage shops, live music venues, and indie culture. Browse the many second-hand clothing and vintage electronics shops. This area represents a very different side of Tokyo's youth culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Shimokitazawa café scene — many unique, independent coffee shops with affordable prices (¥400–¥600 per coffee). Walk through the narrow streets and discover local art galleries, small theaters, and independent bookshops.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Roppongi for the evening. Visit Mori Art Museum (¥1,800) in Roppongi Hills — excellent contemporary art with a free city view from the observation deck. The area transforms at night into a lively entertainment district.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or local café near the hotel for ¥300–¥500.
meals.lunch: Shimokitazawa — try a local curry lunch at a neighborhood restaurant for ¥700–¥900.
meals.dinner: Roppongi — budget ramen or gyoza at a local restaurant away from the tourist traps for ¥700–¥1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is a great place to find affordable vintage tech gadgets and electronics in second-hand shops. Roppongi Hills Mori Art Museum ticket includes access to the Tokyo City View observation deck — great value. Avoid overpriced tourist restaurants in Roppongi.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Koenji — another authentic Tokyo neighborhood popular with locals. Explore the covered shopping arcades (shotengai) and vintage shops. Saturday morning flea markets sometimes appear in the area — check local listings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nakameguro for a scenic afternoon walk along the Meguro River canal. The tree-lined canal is beautiful in spring. Browse the independent boutiques, cafés, and design shops along the riverbank.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) — a stunning architectural bookstore and cultural complex open until midnight. A great example of Japanese design culture. Browse the magazine and tech book sections. Nearby Daikanyama neighborhood has affordable bistros.

meals.breakfast: Koenji — local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) breakfast with toast and egg for ¥400–¥600.
meals.lunch: Nakameguro — grab a bento or sandwich from a local deli along the river for ¥600–¥800.
meals.dinner: Daikanyama — affordable Italian or Japanese fusion restaurant for ¥1,000–¥1,400.

day_by_day.notes: Nakameguro is one of Tokyo's most photogenic neighborhoods. Daikanyama T-Site is a must-visit for design and culture enthusiasts — completely free to browse. Saturday is a great day to observe Tokyo locals in relaxed weekend mode.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300) adjacent to Tsukiji — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond. Take the traditional ferry across to Asakusa (¥800) for a scenic water bus experience on the Sumida River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon in Asakusa for a final deep exploration. Visit Senso-ji Temple complex thoroughly — explore the side streets, smaller shrines, and the Nakamise Street shops for last-minute souvenir shopping at budget prices.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening splurge — visit the Tokyo Skytree (¥2,100 for lower observation deck) for breathtaking night views of the entire Tokyo metropolitan area. Book tickets online in advance to avoid queues. A memorable way to spend the penultimate evening.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — go back to your favorite vendor for a farewell meal, ¥600–¥1,000.
meals.lunch: Asakusa — try a traditional Japanese lunch set (kaiseki-style budget set) for ¥900–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Near Tokyo Skytree — try monjayaki (Tokyo-style savory pancake) at a local restaurant in Asakusa for ¥900–¥1,300.

day_by_day.notes: Book Tokyo Skytree tickets online in advance — it's very popular on Sundays. The water bus from Hamarikyu to Asakusa is a scenic and unique way to travel and see Tokyo from the water. Great for photos.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — last walk through Tsukiji Outer Market to say goodbye to the neighborhood. Pick up any last food souvenirs: packaged dashi stock, nori seaweed, or dried seafood snacks to bring home. These are affordable and pack well.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon exploration — visit any missed spots or revisit favorites. Consider the Ginza Six mall (free to enter) for a final look at Japanese design and food hall (depachika basement food floor — amazing even just to browse). Head back to hotel to pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparations. Enjoy a final budget dinner near the hotel. Reflect on 13 days of Tokyo exploration.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — one last fresh seafood breakfast for ¥600–¥900.
meals.lunch: Ginza Six basement food hall (depachika) — pick up a beautiful bento box for ¥900–¥1,400.
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a local Tsukiji izakaya or ramen shop for ¥700–¥1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is the best place to buy food souvenirs — vacuum-packed dashi, nori, and dried fish are affordable and TSA/customs friendly. Remember to load any remaining balance on your Suica card for transit to the airport. Keep ¥3,000–¥5,000 cash for airport transit and last expenses.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and settle in after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 13:00. Take the Narita Express or Limousine Bus to central Tokyo (approx. 60–90 min). Check in to your Tsukiji boutique hotel, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation stroll around the Tsukiji Outer Market neighborhood to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Tsukiji Outer Market evening stalls and nearby Harumi-dori street. Visit Hamarikyu Gardens for a calming late-afternoon waterfront walk (closes at 17:00 — aim to arrive by 16:00). Wind down with a quiet evening in Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick set meal (teishoku) at a local diner near Tsukiji — try Nakamura-ya or a nearby soba shop for ¥900–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market evening vendors — fresh seafood skewers, tamagoyaki (egg omelette), and grilled scallops. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag is real — keep Day 1 light. Grab a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. Tsukiji Outer Market vendors typically close by 14:00–15:00, so the evening stroll is more about ambiance than shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (jet lag may help!) and visit Tsukiji Outer Market at its peak morning buzz (6:00–9:00 AM). Sample fresh tuna sashimi, tamagoyaki, and uni (sea urchin) from market vendors. This is one of Tokyo's most iconic local food experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara Electric Town (30 min by metro) — the heartland of Tokyo's tech and electronics culture. Browse multi-floor electronics shops like Yodobashi Camera and Akihabara Radio Kaikan, explore retro game shops, and visit the Akihabara UDX tech complex.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara for dinner and explore the neighborhood's unique maid café culture or visit a themed restaurant. Walk through the illuminated neon streets after dark for a quintessential Tokyo tech-culture atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh sashimi breakfast bowl (kaisendon) at Nakajima or Daiwa Sushi-style stalls. ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.lunch: Ramen at a local Akihabara shop — try Fuunji or a nearby tonkotsu spot. ¥900–¥1,300
meals.dinner: Akihabara izakaya (Japanese pub) — order yakitori skewers, edamame, and cold Sapporo beer. ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best before 10:00 AM for freshest produce and shortest queues. In Akihabara, multi-floor electronics stores often have tax-free floors for tourists — bring your passport.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa (20 min from Tsukiji by metro). Arrive early (before 9:00 AM) to beat crowds. Walk Nakamise-dori shopping street for traditional crafts and snacks, and explore the surrounding Asakusa neighborhood on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Tokyo Skytree (adjacent to Asakusa) for panoramic views of Tokyo — the Tembo Deck at 350m is included in mid-range budgets. Then visit the nearby Sumida Aquarium or stroll along the Sumida River promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Asakusa for the Hoppy Street (Hoppy-dori) area — a lively alley of casual izakayas serving affordable food and drinks in a retro shitamachi (old town) atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa Imahan or a local kissaten (coffee shop) near Senso-ji for morning coffee and toast set. ¥600–¥900
meals.lunch: Asakusa Mugitoro — traditional mugitoro gohan (grated yam over rice) or try a tempura set lunch near the temple. ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Hoppy Street izakaya —煮込み (nikomi stew), grilled offal (motsu), and Hoppy beer. Very local and affordable. ¥1,500–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Skytree tickets can be booked online in advance to avoid queues (¥2,100 for Tembo Deck). Asakusa is one of Tokyo's most walkable neighborhoods — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Harajuku — visit Meiji Jingu Shrine in the morning forest setting (free entry, serene atmosphere). Then walk through the wooded Yoyogi Park, which is especially lively on Sundays with musicians and picnickers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down Takeshita Street for quirky youth fashion and crepes, then head to Omotesando for upscale boutique window shopping and architecture (Tadao Ando's Omotesando Hills is worth a look). Visit the Prada and Louis Vuitton flagship buildings as architectural landmarks.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the iconic Shibuya Scramble Crossing experience. Visit the Shibuya Sky rooftop observation deck for sunset views, then explore the area around Shibuya Stream and the revamped Scramble Square.

meals.breakfast: Yoyogi Park area café or Harajuku bakery — try Pain de Campagne or a local depachika (department store basement) pastry. ¥700–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepe from Marion Crepes (a Tokyo institution) plus a bowl of udon at a nearby shop. ¥1,000–�      ¥1,500
meals.dinner: Shibuya — Ichiran Ramen (solo ramen booths, very unique tech-meets-food experience) or a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) at Uobei Shibuya. ¥1,200–¥2,000

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free and open from sunrise to sunset. Shibuya Sky tickets are ¥2,000 — book online in advance. Sunday mornings in Yoyogi Park are a great window into authentic Tokyo local life.

day_by_day.morning: Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets (Toyosu/Odaiba area) — immersive digital art installations that perfectly blend tech culture and creativity. Book tickets in advance as they sell out. teamLab Planets in Toyosu is a 20-min metro ride from Tsukiji.
day_by_day.afternoon: After teamLab, explore Toyosu Market (the successor to Tsukiji's wholesale market). Take a guided observation tour of the tuna auction viewing area or browse the Uogashi Yokocho food stalls inside the market building.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Odaiba via the Yurikamome monorail for futuristic waterfront views. Visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (home to a giant Gundam statue — a tech culture landmark), and enjoy the Rainbow Bridge illuminated at night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area café or convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) — onigiri, tamagoyaki sandwich, and canned coffee. ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Toyosu Market food hall — fresh sushi set or seafood bowl. ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.dinner: Odaiba — Decks Tokyo Beach food floor or a ramen shop in DiverCity. ¥1,500–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets must be booked online in advance (¥3,200–¥3,800). Check the official website for the latest venue status as teamLab Borderless reopened in a new Azabudai Hills location in 2024. Confirm current location before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shinjuku — start with the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free, opens 9:00 AM) for sweeping city views. Then walk through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (especially beautiful in spring with late cherry blossoms or fresh greenery).
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive into Shinjuku's tech and electronics culture at Yodobashi Camera Multimedia Akiba-style stores in West Shinjuku. Then explore the narrow alleys of Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) in East Shinjuku for a pre-dinner atmosphere soak.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Kabukicho — Tokyo's famous entertainment district. Visit Robot Restaurant (book in advance) for a uniquely over-the-top Tokyo tech-entertainment experience, or explore the new Kabukicho Tower complex with its diverse food and entertainment floors.

meals.breakfast: Shinjuku depachika (Isetan or Takashimaya basement) — grab a morning pastry and coffee. ¥700–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen area — bento from a convenience store or nearby teishoku restaurant, enjoyed in the garden. ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — tiny yakitori stalls with grilled chicken skewers, beer, and smoky atmosphere. ¥2,000–¥3,000

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen entry is ¥500. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building North Tower observation deck is free but check for closures. Kabukicho Tower opened in 2023 and has multiple dining floors worth exploring.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (2.5 hours from Shinjuku via Tobu Nikko Line). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — ornate, colorful, and set in cedar forests. Explore Rinno-ji Temple and Yomeimon Gate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko's Shinkyo Bridge and surrounding nature. If time allows, take a bus to Kegon Falls (97m waterfall) and Lake Chuzenji for mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Arrive back in Tsukiji by 19:00–20:00. Have a relaxed dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab an ekiben (train station bento) at Shinjuku Station before boarding. ¥900–¥1,400
meals.lunch: Nikko — yuba (tofu skin) cuisine, a local specialty. Try Gyoshintei or a local restaurant near Tosho-gu. ¥1,500–¥2,500
meals.dinner: Back in Tsukiji — a quiet sushi or ramen dinner near the hotel. ¥1,500–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Tobu Nikko All Area Pass for unlimited buses in Nikko (¥2,000–¥4,500 depending on scope). Tosho-gu entry is ¥1,300. Nikko can be busy on weekdays — arrive early to beat tour groups.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ginza — Tokyo's most prestigious shopping and cultural district, a 10-minute walk from Tsukiji. Visit the Itoya stationery flagship store (9 floors of beautifully curated paper goods and design), the Ginza Six complex, and the free Hermès Maison des Métiers d'Art gallery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi (30 min from Ginza by metro) for contemporary art with a tech and global perspective. The attached Tokyo City View observation deck offers excellent views. Then explore the Roppongi Hills complex.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through Azabudai Hills — Tokyo's newest landmark development (opened 2023) featuring futuristic architecture, galleries, and the Japan's tallest building. Grab dinner in one of its many restaurant options.

meals.breakfast: Ginza area kissaten — a classic Japanese coffee shop breakfast (morning set: toast, egg, coffee). ¥600–¥900
meals.lunch: Ginza Six basement food hall — high-quality bento, sushi rolls, or wagyu beef sandwiches. ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Azabudai Hills — choose from Japanese, Italian, or Asian fusion options in the complex's diverse restaurant floors. ¥2,500–¥4,000

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum entry is ¥1,800 and includes Tokyo City View. Ginza is walkable from your Tsukiji hotel — enjoy the morning stroll. Azabudai Hills is also home to teamLab Borderless (new location) if not visited on Day 5.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhoods (shitamachi). Stroll through Yanaka Cemetery (beautiful with spring foliage), explore Yanaka Ginza shopping street for traditional crafts and street food, and soak in the Edo-era atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ueno — visit the Tokyo National Museum (Japan's largest museum, covering Japanese art and history). Then stroll through Ueno Park and visit Ameyoko Market — a lively open-air market street with food, fashion, and local energy.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Koenji or Shimokitazawa (30 min by metro) — Tokyo's bohemian neighborhoods known for vintage shops, live music, and local izakayas. Great for experiencing non-touristy Tokyo nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza — fresh melon bread, croquettes, and coffee from local bakeries and shops. ¥600–¥900
meals.lunch: Ueno Ameyoko — street food lunch: yakitori, Korean-style fried chicken, fresh fruit. ¥800–¥1,500
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa — a local izakaya or curry restaurant. Shimokitazawa has excellent affordable dining options. ¥1,500–¥2,500

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo National Museum entry is ¥1,000. Yanaka is best explored on foot — pick up a free map at the Yanaka Information Center. Shimokitazawa is famous for its live music venues if you want an evening show.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Sony Park or Sony Showroom in Ginza (free) to explore cutting-edge Sony tech products and interactive exhibits. Then walk to the Panasonic Wonder Life-BOX or visit the Canon Digital House in Ginza for more tech culture immersion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kanda and Jimbocho — Tokyo's famous book and electronics district. Jimbocho is lined with hundreds of used bookstores and is a beloved local institution. Nearby Kanda has excellent traditional soba restaurants.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Nihonbashi — a historic commercial district near Tsukiji. Visit Coredo Muromachi for upscale Japanese food shopping and dining, and stroll along the Nihonbashi bridge area, beautifully lit in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or Ginza café — coffee and a morning pastry. ¥600–¥900
meals.lunch: Kanda — traditional soba (buckwheat noodles) at a century-old soba-ya. Try Kanda Yabu Soba (a Tokyo institution). ¥1,200–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Nihonbashi Coredo Muromachi — Japanese cuisine set meal (kaiseki-lite) or a high-quality tonkatsu (pork cutlet) restaurant. ¥2,000–¥3,500

day_by_day.notes: Kanda Yabu Soba is a historic restaurant — arrive early as it gets busy. Jimbocho bookstores are open on weekends. Nihonbashi is a 10-minute walk from your Tsukiji hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (1 hour from Tokyo Station via JR Yokosuka Line). Visit the Great Buddha (Kotoku-in, ¥300) and Hase-dera Temple with its coastal views. Explore the bamboo groves and quiet temple paths.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Komachi-dori shopping street for local snacks (try shirasu rice bowls — a Kamakura specialty) and crafts. Visit Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine — Kamakura's most important shrine. Hike the Daibutsu Hiking Trail if energy allows.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the Tsukiji/Ginza area. Consider a final evening walk along the Sumida River waterfront near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departing Tokyo Station. ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Kamakura — shirasu don (whitebait rice bowl) at a local restaurant near Hase Station. ¥1,200–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Tsukiji/Ginza area — a relaxed sushi dinner or yakitori set. ¥2,000–¥3,000

day_by_day.notes: Use a JR Pass or purchase a Suica-compatible ticket for Kamakura. The round trip from Tokyo is approximately ¥1,940. Kamakura is best on weekday mornings — Sunday can be busy, so start early.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shiodome and Hamarikyu Gardens (5-minute walk from hotel) — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a teahouse on a tidal pond, surrounded by modern skyscrapers. Take the traditional ferry boat across to Asakusa for a scenic river cruise (¥1,020).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Panasonic Shiodome Museum or the Advertising Museum Tokyo (AdMT) in Shiodome — a fascinating free museum showcasing Japanese advertising and media history, a unique lens into Japanese consumer tech culture. Then explore the Caretta Shiodome mall.
day_by_day.evening: Final major dinner experience — splurge slightly at a mid-to-upper range restaurant. Consider a kaiseki-lite dinner at a Ginza restaurant or an omakase sushi counter experience (book in advance). This is your second-to-last evening — celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hamarikyu Gardens teahouse — matcha and wagashi (traditional sweets) by the pond. ¥1,000–¥1,500 (includes garden entry at ¥300)
meals.lunch: Shiodome area — a business lunch set at one of the tower restaurants (many offer affordable lunch sets). ¥1,200–¥1,800
meals.dinner: Ginza or Tsukiji — omakase sushi counter or high-quality tempura restaurant. ¥4,000–¥6,000 per person (a worthy splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens entry is ¥300. The Sumida River ferry to Asakusa is a lovely way to see Tokyo from the water. Book the evening restaurant in advance — mid-range omakase counters fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — return to Tsukiji Outer Market one last time for a farewell breakfast. Pick up any food souvenirs: dried seafood, tamagoyaki molds, nori (seaweed), or dashi packs. Also visit a nearby convenience store for snacks to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Ginza Itoya (stationery and design gifts), or visit a Don Quijote (Donki) store for affordable tech gadgets, beauty products, and Japanese snacks. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport (Narita or Haneda) — allow 2–3 hours before departure. Enjoy a final airport ramen or soba at the terminal before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — one last fresh sashimi bowl or tamagoyaki and green tea. ¥1,000–¥1,800
meals.lunch: Ginza depachika bento or a conveyor belt sushi lunch — light and easy before travel. ¥1,200–¥2,000
meals.dinner: Airport terminal — Ichiran Ramen (available at Narita Terminal 2) or a soba restaurant in the departure lounge. ¥1,000–¥1,800

day_by_day.notes: Leave for the airport by 15:00–16:00 to allow ample time for check-in and security. Narita Express from Tokyo Station takes 60 min (¥3,070). Haneda is closer — 30 min by monorail or Keikyu Line. Don't forget to claim consumption tax refunds at the airport for eligible purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the legendary Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, and matcha treats from local vendors. Engage with longtime merchants and discover the heart of Tokyo's food culture in one of the world's most famous market districts.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tokyo (flight LH lands at 13:00) — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to boutique stay in Tsukiji, Chuo City via private luxury car service (pre-booked). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your premium accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely first stroll through the Tsukiji Outer Market to get your bearings. Sample fresh tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), grilled seafood skewers, and premium tuna nigiri from iconic stalls. This serves as both an orientation walk and your first taste of Tokyo's legendary food culture.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Saito (or equivalent Michelin-starred omakase restaurant in Ginza, a short taxi ride away). Experience the pinnacle of Edomae sushi with a 12–15 course chef's omakase. Afterwards, take a night walk along the Sumida River waterfront near Tsukiji for a tranquil introduction to the city.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light snacks and street food tastings at Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh uni, otoro sashimi, and tamagoyaki from premium stalls
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred omakase sushi in Ginza (e.g., Sushi Yoshitake or Sushi Saito) — budget ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep the schedule relaxed to recover from the flight. Pre-arrange private airport transfer for a seamless luxury arrival. Confirm omakase reservation well in advance as top Tokyo sushi counters book months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour (featured experience): Join a guided premium food tour of the legendary Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, grilled seafood skewers, premium dashi broths, and seasonal Japanese pickles. Learn the history of the market from a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to the Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning Edo-period landscape garden with a traditional teahouse on the water. Enjoy a formal matcha tea ceremony experience with wagashi (Japanese sweets). Then explore the adjacent Shiodome district and visit the Panasonic Center or teamLab's digital art installations for an early taste of Tokyo's tech-meets-art culture.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ginza Six's top-floor restaurant or Kyubey Ginza — a legendary sushi institution beloved by Tokyo's elite. After dinner, explore Ginza's luxury boutiques and illuminated streets for a quintessential upscale Tokyo evening.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast set at the hotel or a nearby kissaten (traditional coffee shop) — tamago gohan, miso soup, grilled fish, and pickles
meals.lunch: Premium street food during the Tsukiji food tour — fresh oysters, sea urchin, and sashimi platters
meals.dinner: Kyubey Ginza or a Ginza kaiseki restaurant — budget ¥20,000–¥40,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tsukiji food tour in advance for a private or small-group premium experience. The Hamarikyu teahouse requires a small entry fee. Ginza is walkable from Tsukiji — approximately 15 minutes on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Akihabara — Tokyo's iconic Electric Town — for an immersive deep dive into tech culture. Visit multi-story electronics megastores (Yodobashi Camera, Akihabara Radio Kaikan) to explore the latest gadgets, robotics kits, and cutting-edge tech. Browse specialty stores for rare components and futuristic consumer electronics unavailable outside Japan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) on Odaiba island, accessible via the futuristic Yurikamome automated monorail. Interact with ASIMO-successor robots, explore AI and space technology exhibits, and experience immersive digital installations. Afterwards, explore the Odaiba waterfront with views of Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo Bay.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Narisawa in Minami-Aoyama — one of Asia's 50 Best Restaurants, renowned for its innovative 'Satoyama Cuisine' blending Japanese nature philosophy with avant-garde technique. A truly world-class culinary experience.

meals.breakfast: Artisan bakery breakfast at Maison Landemaine or similar premium bakery near Tsukiji/Ginza
meals.lunch: Ramen at Fuunji or a premium tonkotsu counter in Akihabara — or a bento set from a high-end depachika (department store basement food hall)
meals.dinner: Narisawa, Minami-Aoyama — 2 Michelin stars, budget ¥35,000–¥55,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays. The Yurikamome monorail ride itself is a scenic tech experience worth savoring. Book Narisawa at least 2–3 months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Toyosu Market (the successor to the original Tsukiji wholesale market) for a behind-the-scenes look at the world's largest fish market. Book a premium observation tour to watch the legendary tuna auction from the viewing gallery. Witness the extraordinary scale of Tokyo's seafood supply chain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Shibuya and Harajuku for a cultural contrast. Visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck for panoramic city views. Then explore Omotesando — Tokyo's most architecturally refined shopping boulevard — visiting flagship stores designed by Tadao Ando, Herzog & de Meuron, and SANAA. Browse the Omotesando Hills complex for premium Japanese fashion and design.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Florilège in Minami-Aoyama — a celebrated French-Japanese fusion restaurant with 2 Michelin stars, known for open-kitchen theater dining and impeccable seasonal ingredients. A perfect blend of global technique and local produce.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the Toyosu tuna auction (auction viewing typically begins around 5:30–6:30 AM; adjust schedule accordingly)
meals.lunch: Sushi breakfast/brunch at Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi within Toyosu Market — widely considered the best sushi breakfast in the world
meals.dinner: Florilège, Minami-Aoyama — 2 Michelin stars, budget ¥25,000–¥40,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tuna auction viewing at Toyosu requires advance lottery registration through the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market website — apply months ahead. Alternatively, the viewing gallery (no lottery required) opens at 5:45 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic Yanaka district — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Wander narrow lanes lined with traditional wooden houses, artisan workshops, and independent food stalls. Visit Yanaka Cemetery (beautiful during late cherry blossom season in mid-April) and browse the Yanaka Ginza shotengai (retro shopping street).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno — Japan's largest and oldest museum, housing extraordinary collections of samurai armor, ancient ceramics, Buddhist sculpture, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints. Opt for a private guided tour to gain deeper cultural context. Then stroll through Ueno Park.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Kanda in Minami-Aoyama — a legendary 3 Michelin star kaiseki restaurant by Chef Hiroyuki Kanda, offering an extraordinary multi-course journey through Japan's seasonal cuisine with exquisite plating and precision.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast at a local Yanaka kissaten or the hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Yanaka neighborhood restaurant — handmade soba, grilled yakitori, or seasonal Japanese home cooking
meals.dinner: Restaurant Kanda — 3 Michelin stars, budget ¥40,000–¥60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays. Book Restaurant Kanda well in advance — reservations are extremely competitive.

day_by_day.morning: Visit teamLab Planets in Toyosu — an immersive digital art museum where technology and nature merge in breathtaking walk-through installations. Experience rooms filled with infinite crystal universes, floating flowers, and mirror-reflected light fields. This is one of the world's most celebrated intersections of art and technology.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Shibuya for a visit to the Google Japan office area and the QWS (Shibuya Quest) innovation hub at Shibuya Scramble Square. Explore the upper floors of Scramble Square for panoramic views and cutting-edge co-working/startup culture. Visit the Scramble Square observation deck 'Shibuya Sky' if not visited earlier.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Sho in Yotsuya — an intimate, legendary counter-style sushi restaurant famed for its creative omakase that goes beyond traditional nigiri. One of the most coveted reservations in Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Premium hotel breakfast or brunch at a Tsukiji-area café with fresh seafood options
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Toyosu/Shibuya premium ramen or tonkatsu restaurant — try Maisen Tonkatsu in Omotesando for premium pork cutlet
meals.dinner: Sushi Sho, Yotsuya — highly exclusive omakase, budget ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab Planets tickets online in advance — timed entry slots sell out quickly, especially on weekends. Sushi Sho reservations require a Japanese-speaking contact or hotel concierge assistance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — a UNESCO World Heritage Site approximately 2 hours from Tokyo by Tobu Limited Express (book a premium Green Car seat). Explore the elaborately decorated Toshogu Shrine, Rinnoji Temple, and Futarasan Shrine set among ancient cedar forests. Nikko represents the apex of Edo-period decorative architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko's Shinkyo Sacred Bridge and Kanmangafuchi Abyss — a serene riverside path lined with Jizo stone statues. Enjoy the peaceful mountain atmosphere before heading back to Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by late afternoon. Dinner at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten in Ginza — the world-famous 3 Michelin star sushi restaurant made legendary by the documentary 'Jiro Dreams of Sushi.' An unparalleled 20-minute omakase that is the pinnacle of sushi craftsmanship.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departing for Nikko
meals.lunch: Yuba (tofu skin) cuisine lunch at a traditional Nikko restaurant — a regional specialty unique to the area
meals.dinner: Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten, Ginza — 3 Michelin stars, budget ¥40,000–¥55,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Sukiyabashi Jiro is notoriously difficult to book — reservations must be made through the hotel concierge and require a Japanese credit card guarantee. The experience lasts approximately 20–30 minutes. Nikko can be cold in April — bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku for a morning exploration of Kabukicho and the Golden Gai district (atmospheric even in daylight). Then visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck for free panoramic views of the city including Mount Fuji on clear days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — one of Japan's most beautiful parks, especially magnificent in mid-to-late April with late cherry blossoms and early spring flowers. Visit the French formal garden, Japanese traditional garden, and greenhouse. Afterwards, browse Isetan Shinjuku — Japan's most prestigious department store — for premium Japanese fashion, cosmetics, and the extraordinary basement food hall.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Tempura Kondo in Ginza — a 2 Michelin star tempura restaurant where Chef Fumio Kondo elevates vegetables and seafood to extraordinary heights through masterful frying technique. Followed by cocktails at the New York Bar atop the Park Hyatt Shinjuku (made famous by 'Lost in Translation').

meals.breakfast: Artisan coffee and pastries at Fuglen Tokyo or Blue Bottle Coffee in Shinjuku area
meals.lunch: Premium bento from Isetan Shinjuku's depachika basement food hall — extraordinary variety of top-tier prepared foods
meals.dinner: Tempura Kondo, Ginza — 2 Michelin stars, budget ¥25,000–¥40,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen requires an entry fee and is closed on Mondays. The New York Bar has a cover charge in the evenings — reservations recommended for window seats with city views.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Sony Park and Sony Showroom in Ginza for an immersive showcase of Sony's latest innovations — spatial audio, 8K displays, professional cameras, and concept technology. Then explore the Itoya stationery flagship store — a 12-floor luxury stationery and design emporium that is a cultural landmark of Ginza.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Shibuya's Daikanyama neighborhood — Tokyo's most refined residential district. Visit Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) — an architecturally stunning premium bookstore and lifestyle complex beloved by Tokyo's creative elite. Browse curated books, vinyl records, and design objects. Stroll to neighboring Nakameguro along the cherry blossom-lined canal.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at L'Effervescence in Nishi-Azabu — a 2 Michelin star restaurant by Chef Shinobu Namae, blending French technique with deep Japanese philosophy and hyper-seasonal local ingredients. One of Tokyo's most intellectually engaging dining experiences.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast at a Tsukiji-area traditional restaurant — grilled fish, rice, miso soup, and pickles
meals.lunch: Artisan lunch at a Daikanyama café or Log Road Daikanyama's premium restaurant options
meals.dinner: L'Effervescence, Nishi-Azabu — 2 Michelin stars, budget ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Sony Showroom is free to enter. Daikanyama T-Site is open until 2 AM — a perfect rainy-day option. Nakameguro canal is particularly beautiful with late cherry blossoms in mid-April.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills — one of Tokyo's most prestigious contemporary art museums with rotating exhibitions featuring global and Japanese artists. Combine with the Tokyo City View observation deck for sweeping 360-degree city panoramas. Explore the Roppongi Hills complex — a landmark of urban tech-meets-culture development.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Art Center Tokyo in Roppongi — Japan's largest exhibition space with striking architectural design by Kisho Kurokawa. Then explore 21_21 Design Sight in Midtown Roppongi — a design museum co-founded by Issey Miyake and Tadao Ando, celebrating the intersection of design, technology, and everyday life.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ryugin in Roppongi — a legendary 3 Michelin star kaiseki restaurant by Chef Seiji Yamamoto, renowned for using cutting-edge culinary science to reimagine traditional Japanese cuisine. Followed by sophisticated cocktails at the Roppongi Hills Club bar.

meals.breakfast: Premium breakfast at the hotel or a Ginza patisserie
meals.lunch: Lunch at Roppongi Hills' premium restaurant floor — options include high-end soba, wagyu beef, or Japanese-French fusion
meals.dinner: Nihonryori Ryugin, Roppongi — 3 Michelin stars, budget ¥40,000–¥60,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Mori Art Museum is closed on Tuesdays. Book Ryugin well in advance — it ranks among Asia's 50 Best Restaurants. The combined Mori Art Museum + Tokyo City View ticket offers excellent value.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Hakone — approximately 85 minutes from Shinjuku on the Romancecar (Odakyu's luxury limited express train, book a premium seat). Arrive at Hakone and take the Hakone Ropeway for aerial views of Mount Fuji and the volcanic Owakudani valley. Visit the Hakone Open-Air Museum — a world-class sculpture park featuring works by Picasso, Rodin, and Henry Moore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hakone Museum of Art for extraordinary Japanese ceramics and gardens. Enjoy a traditional Japanese onsen (hot spring) experience at a premium ryokan day-use facility — Hakone Kowakien Yunessun or the exclusive Gora Kadan for a private onsen session with Mount Fuji views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Dinner at Quintessence in Shirokane — a 3 Michelin star French restaurant by Chef Shuzo Kishida, celebrated for minimalist precision and extraordinary ingredient sourcing. One of the most refined dining experiences in Japan.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departing for Hakone
meals.lunch: Traditional Japanese lunch at a Hakone ryokan restaurant — kaiseki-style with seasonal mountain vegetables and fresh river fish
meals.dinner: Quintessence, Shirokane — 3 Michelin stars, budget ¥35,000–¥55,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Check Mount Fuji visibility forecasts before the trip — clear days are most common in early morning. The Romancecar Vista EX train offers the best views. Book Gora Kadan's day-use onsen in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Asakusa — Tokyo's most atmospheric historic district. Explore Senso-ji Temple at dawn for a serene, crowd-free experience. Browse the Nakamise shopping street for premium traditional crafts, lacquerware, and wagashi sweets. Visit the Kappabashi 'Kitchen Town' district for professional Japanese culinary tools and ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sumida Hokusai Museum near Asakusa — dedicated to the legendary ukiyo-e master Katsushika Hokusai, with immersive digital recreations of his iconic works. Then cross the Azuma Bridge to Skytree Town and ascend the Tokyo Skytree — the world's second-tallest structure — to the premium Tembo Galleria at 450 meters for extraordinary views.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Saito in Azabu-Juban or a final premium omakase of your choice — alternatively, a private chef's table experience arranged through the hotel concierge. End the evening with a rooftop cocktail at a Ginza or Marunouchi sky bar, toasting to an extraordinary Tokyo journey.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Asakusa breakfast — fresh ningyo-yaki (character-shaped cakes), amazake (sweet rice drink), and street food from Nakamise
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sometaro — a historic Asakusa okonomiyaki restaurant — or premium tempura at Daikokuya Tempura in Asakusa
meals.dinner: Premium farewell omakase or kaiseki dinner — budget ¥30,000–¥60,000 per person depending on venue

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is most magical at 6–7 AM before crowds arrive. Tokyo Skytree tickets can be purchased in advance online to skip queues. Consider purchasing premium Japanese knives or ceramics at Kappabashi as luxury souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — take a peaceful walk along the Sumida River waterfront near Tsukiji for a last look at the neighborhood that has been your home base. Visit the nearby Hamarikyu Gardens one final time for a serene matcha tea moment. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping at Ginza — visit Wako department store (Ginza's most iconic luxury retailer), Mikimoto Pearl, and the Ginza Six basement food hall for premium Japanese food souvenirs: high-grade matcha, artisan wagashi, premium sake, and dried seafood. Transfer to airport via private luxury car service.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of world-class cuisine, cutting-edge technology, and the seamless coexistence of ancient tradition and futuristic innovation that makes Tokyo uniquely extraordinary.

meals.breakfast: Final Japanese breakfast at the hotel — savor every last bite of miso soup, grilled fish, and steamed rice
meals.lunch: Premium bento from Ginza Six or Mitsukoshi Ginza's depachika to enjoy at the airport lounge
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or on-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–3.5 hours before departure for Tokyo airport transfers (Narita: 60–90 min; Haneda: 30–45 min by premium car). Ginza Six basement food hall is one of the best places in Tokyo for premium food souvenirs. Consider Japan's tax-free shopping refund at the airport for purchases made during the trip.
